title: 207. What Research Says About DEPRESSION feat. Dr. Steven Hollon
description_html: Today's guest is Dr. Steven D. Hollon— the Gertrude Conaway Vanderbilt Professor of Psychology at Vanderbilt University. His work focuses on the etiology and treatment of depression in adults, with his research showing that cognitive and behavioral interventions for depression can be as efficacious as and more enduring than antidepressant medications.
talk_about: + Why Dr. Hollon became interested in studying depression
mentioned_html:
+ ABCT

+ Dr. Hollon's Research

+ Mind Over Mood

+ "What we got wrong about depression..."

+ Seligman & Maier on learned helplessness
guests: dr. steven hollon, professor of psychology at vanderbilt university
summary: sadie sits down with dr. steven hollon, a leading depression researcher at vanderbilt, to talk about what the science actually tells us about depression. they cover how common depression really is (way more than we thought), why it might be an evolved response rather than just a broken brain, and what makes cognitive behavioral therapy so effective. dr. hollon explains why some people have one depressive episode while others have many, why adolescence is such a vulnerable time, and two practical things anyone can do when depression hits: don't wait to feel like doing something before you do it, and don't believe everything you think. the conversation is research-heavy but accessible, offering real clarity on how depression works and what helps.
quote: depression is a disease of expectation and recollection. it lives in the future and in the past. at the moment, it's not that you can't enjoy; it's that you don't think you will.
quote_display: depression is a disease of EXPECTATION and RECOLLECTION. it lives in the FUTURE and in the PAST. at the moment, it's not that you can't enjoy; it's that you don't think you WILL.
